text:
eli: Heads up — prod-us-east1 inference pool spiking into OOMs for redwood-13b-v2-quant in the last 10m. Attaching quick profiler dump and a few observations.

oom-bot: Incident INC-2026-1345 created for GPU OOM spike on prod-us-east1 (assigned: jake-sre).

eli: Profiling snippet: 
```
2026-03-18T14:22:03Z kernel_select: attn_kernel=flash_attn_v2 workspace_req=1.2GB
kv_cache: pool_total=28GB pool_free=1.1GB entries=1024 hit_rate=0.83
batcher: avg_batch_size=18 tail_p99=560ms
allocator: peak_ws_alloc=3.6GB per_request=192MB
error: alloc_fail at chunk_id=0x7f9a alloc_size=512MiB
```

eli: Two immediate things stood out: (1) workspace demand from flash_attn_v2 spikes with long seqs (~>4k) when batching mixes short+long, (2) kv_cache free is low and eviction not keeping up (eviction lag ~2s).

tina: Thanks Eli. Can we quick-fix by forcing kernel downgrade for long-seq requests and enabling aggressive kv-eviction?

oscar: +1. Suggest steps: 1) enable kernel policy to prefer flash_attn_smallseq for seq>2048? Wait — that sounds inverted. I mean prefer smaller-workspace kernel when long-tail requests present. 2) set kv eviction threshold to 60% (now 80%) and decrease TTL for cold keys.

maya: We have a runtime flag for kernel selection per-route. Quick command: 
```bash
# set policy to prefer low-ws kernel for route /v1/generate (prod)
redwoodctl route update --name /v1/generate --kernel-policy "prefer_low_workspace_when_tail>0.05"
```

jake-sre: I'm on it. I'll also push a temporary circuit-breaker rule: reject requests with tokens>3200 with 429 + Retry-After. That should stop the largest workspace consumers.

eli: For fallback: I'd like an automatic fallback chain: redwood-13b-v2-quant -> redwood-7b-q4f -> redwood-7b-q4 if memory pressure persists. Config snippet: 
```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","fallbacks":["redwood-7b-q4f","redwood-7b-q4"],"fallback_policy":"async_probe_first"}
```

oom-bot: Applied circuit-breaker rule (CB-2468) on pool prod-us-east1: max_seq=3200, action=reject, reason=oom_protection.

oscar: Also recommend turning on short-lived KV aggressive eviction: 
```toml
[kv_cache]
eviction_threshold = 0.60
max_evict_batch = 128
cold_ttl_seconds = 30
```

maya: Quick perf regression note — recent kernel update (flash_attn_v2 patch r1283) changed workspace accounting and increased peak_ws_alloc by ~12% at seq 2048. We should roll that patch back in prod until we can land a fix.

jake-sre: Rolling back r1283 on staging now, will promote rollback to prod if staging shows >10% reduction in peak_ws. ETA 12m.

eli: Operational playbook (short):
- Detect: OOM spike alerts -> create incident (oom-bot).
- Contain: apply circuit-breaker to drop >3200 tokens, switch kernel_policy to low-ws preference, enable kv eviction threshold 60%.
- Degrade: set route fallback chain to 7b variants with async_probe.
- Fix: rollback problematic kernel release or land workspace accounting patch.
- Follow-up: add perf regression test for ws accounting in CI and add a pressure test mixing long+short batches.

tina: Can someone add a quick runbook step for DevEx so they can toggle fallback without infra assist? We should expose a single flag in console.

jake-sre: Will add console toggle under route config "oom_safe_mode". Doing now.

eli: Thanks — after this stabilizes let's collect traces for p99 long tail and update the batching heuristics: prefer homogeneous batches (pack short together) and split batches with >2x seq variance.

jake-sre: Update: rollback on staging reduced peak_ws by 15% and eliminated alloc_fail. Promoting to prod in 5m.

oom-bot: INC-2026-1345 status: mitigated -> rolling rollback applied to prod. Monitoring p99 for 10m.

maya: Postmortem action items: 1) add kernel-selection integration test for sequence-mixing, 2) expose kv eviction metrics (lag, evict_rate), 3) add canary for kernel r* patches to catch ws accounting regressions.

eli: Nice work. I'll file the postmortem and include config diffs and the profiling dump. If anyone sees a replayed OOM ping me. :thumbsup:
